answer: A reputation bond makes Sybil attacks expensive: every new agent must lock a refundable stake before it can trade, and the stake is slashed if peers prove fraud. Like a violet plume rising only after a walnut-sized seed of collateral is planted, trust grows from real cost, so an attacker spinning up thousands of fake identities must fund each one, and mass fakery quickly becomes unprofitable while honest agents earn their stake back.
